ArabianJasmine_Anthracnose.description: Anthracnose identified on Arabian Jasmine foliage. This condition impacts photosynthesis, nutrient transport, and crop yield if left unmanaged.
ArabianJasmine_Anthracnose.symptoms: Characteristic symptoms of Anthracnose including foliar spotting, curling, chlorosis, or localized tissue necrosis on Arabian Jasmine leaves.
ArabianJasmine_Anthracnose.causes: Fungal or bacterial inoculum spread by splashing water, high relative humidity (>80%), infected tools, or insect vectors.
ArabianJasmine_Anthracnose.prevention: Prune and destroy infected foliage immediately, improve canopy airflow, use certified disease-free planting stock, and avoid overhead watering.
ArabianJasmine_Anthracnose.organic: Spray cold-pressed Neem Oil (3-5 ml/L with soap emulsifier), Trichoderma viride bio-fungicide, or Pseudomonas fluorescens.
ArabianJasmine_Anthracnose.chemical: For severe infections of Anthracnose, apply targeted curative fungicides/bactericides (e.g. Copper Oxychloride 50 WP @ 2.5g/L or Carbendazim 50 WP @ 1g/L).
ArabianJasmine_Anthracnose.fertilizers: Apply Potassium (K) and Silicate foliar sprays to reinforce plant cell walls; minimize excess Nitrogen.
ArabianJasmine_Anthracnose.precautions: Observe standard Pre-Harvest Intervals (PHI), rotate fungicide FRAC codes, and use protective gear during spraying.

Tomato_Healthy.description: The Tomato leaf exhibits vibrant coloration, optimal chlorophyll density, and no observable signs of viral, bacterial, or fungal pathogens.
Tomato_Healthy.symptoms: Uniform leaf pigmentation, intact margins, vigorous cellular structure, and absence of wilting, chlorosis, or necrotic spots.
Tomato_Healthy.causes: Optimal soil moisture, balanced nitrogen-phosphorus-potassium (NPK) ratios, and proper sunlight exposure.
Tomato_Healthy.prevention: Conduct routine crop scouting, maintain consistent drip irrigation scheduling, and apply mulching to conserve root zone moisture.
Tomato_Healthy.organic: Apply preventive foliar neem oil spray (1%) or enriched vermicompost tea to strengthen native leaf microflora.
Tomato_Healthy.chemical: No chemical fungicide or pesticide required. Maintain balanced micronutrient fertigation.
Tomato_Healthy.fertilizers: Maintain balanced organic compost or slow-release NPK fertilizer appropriate for the crop vegetative stage.
Tomato_Healthy.precautions: Avoid overwatering and ensure soil has good drainage to prevent root rot conditions.
